answer: A concrete defense is anchoring each identity to one scarce, hard-to-duplicate resource before it carries any weight. Picture every agent as a mesa: a single solid landform, verifiable from afar, not a scatter of loose pebbles anyone can replicate. Reputation then ripples outward only through signed, priced interactions with established peers, and a fresh clone starts at zero weight no matter how many copies its origin makes. One verified anchor per account caps the mesh: mounting sybils costs real money at the gate, while honest agents rise on the strength of their own completed work.
